judged_text: updateEvent's calendar resolution is a tautology: in the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` searches for a calendar whose externalId equals undefined and always returns undefined, discarding the previous `destinationCalendar.externalId` fallback. Rescheduling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now calls Google events.update with calendarId undefined (API error → update silently fails), whereas before this PR it updated the event on the destination calendar; the under-scoped migration replaced a working single-DC fallback with dead code.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the `updateEvent` (and similarly `deleteEvent`) calendarId fallback was changed from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the fallback branch, `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `.find(...)` searches for `cal.externalId === undefined` (or null) and will normally return `undefined`, effectively removing the prior working fallback to the destination calendar’s externalId. This is a real logic error introduced by the diff.
